title: Chapter 2 Quiz: Spring Core & Dependency Injection
description: Test your knowledge of IoC, DI, beans, scopes, and lifecycle.

questions.question: What does IoC stand for?
questions.explanation: IoC stands for Inversion of Control – a design principle where the control of object creation and lifecycle is transferred to a container.

questions.question: In Spring Boot, the default IoC container is BeanFactory.
questions.explanation: Spring Boot uses ApplicationContext, which is a more powerful container that extends BeanFactory.

questions.question: Which annotation is used to mark a class as a Spring bean in the service layer?
questions.explanation: @Service is a specialization of @Component used for service layer beans.

questions.question: Constructor injection is the preferred way to inject dependencies in modern Spring applications.
questions.explanation: Constructor injection promotes immutability and is easier to test, making it the recommended approach.

questions.question: The annotation that tells Spring to automatically wire dependencies is _________.
questions.explanation: @Autowired is Spring’s annotation for automatic dependency injection.

questions.question: What is the default bean scope in Spring?
questions.explanation: The default scope is singleton – one instance per Spring container.

questions.question: A prototype bean is created once and reused for all injections.
questions.explanation: A prototype bean gets a new instance every time it is requested (injected or looked up).

questions.question: Which method annotation is used to run code after a bean’s dependencies are injected?
questions.explanation: @PostConstruct is a JSR‑250 annotation that Spring supports for initialization logic after dependency injection.

questions.question: The package that Spring Boot scans by default is the package containing the class annotated with _________.
questions.explanation: @SpringBootApplication triggers component scanning starting from the package of the annotated class.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of Dependency Injection?
questions.explanation: DI does not automatically optimize performance; it improves modularity, testability, and flexibility.

questions.question: You can use @Autowired on a constructor even if there is only one constructor.
questions.explanation: You can, but it’s optional – Spring will inject the single constructor automatically.

questions.question: Which scope is appropriate for a bean that holds user‑specific data in a web application?
questions.explanation: Session scope keeps one bean instance per HTTP session, ideal for user‑specific data.

questions.question: The annotation that tells Spring to clean up resources before a bean is destroyed is _________.
questions.explanation: @PreDestroy is used for cleanup methods that run when the container is shutting down.

questions.question: What does the term 'wiring' refer to in Spring?
questions.explanation: Wiring is the process of linking beans together, i.e., injecting dependencies.

questions.question: Field injection (using @Autowired directly on a field) is considered the most testable approach.
questions.explanation: Field injection makes unit testing harder because you cannot easily provide mocks without reflection; constructor injection is preferred for testability.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to declare a bean with a custom name?
questions.explanation: You can specify a custom bean name in any stereotype annotation or @Bean.

questions.question: The ApplicationContext is a sub‑interface of _________.
questions.explanation: ApplicationContext extends BeanFactory, adding enterprise‑specific functionality.

questions.question: What happens if you have two beans of the same type and use @Autowired on a field?
options: Both are injected into a collection
questions.explanation: By default, Spring can’t decide which bean to inject and will throw an exception. You need to use @Primary or @Qualifier to resolve ambiguity.

questions.question: Spring Boot automatically registers a bean for any class annotated with @Component even if it’s outside the main package.
questions.explanation: Component scanning only happens within the main package and its sub‑packages unless you explicitly add @ComponentScan.

questions.question: What is the purpose of @Repository?
options: It marks a class as a REST controller
It marks a class as a data access object and adds persistence exception translation
It marks a class as a service
It marks a class as a configuration
questions.explanation: @Repository is used for DAO classes; it also enables Spring to translate technology‑specific exceptions (like SQLException) into Spring’s DataAccessException hierarchy.
